title: Serbian for English speakers
contentStage: Expanded A1 path with translation word banks, target-language sentence completion, listening and checkpoints

units.title: First conversations
units.subtitle: Greet, introduce yourself, and read familiar words
outcomes: Introduce yourself and ask a name
Read familiar words in both Serbian scripts

theory.title: Two ways to write Serbian
theory.body: Serbian is written in Latin and Cyrillic. Zdravo and Здраво sound the same and both mean hello.

challenges.explanation: Dobar dan is a polite daytime greeting.

theory.title: Introduce yourself
theory.body: Ja sam means “I am.” Zovem se means “my name is.” In Cyrillic these are Ја сам and Зовем се.

challenges.explanation: Zovem se is a natural way to give your name.
Use this informal question to ask a name.
Ja sam is written Ја сам in Cyrillic.
You heard Ja sam, meaning I am.

theory.title: Small words, big impact
theory.body: Molim means “please” and can also mean “you are welcome.” Izvini is an informal “sorry” or “excuse me.”

challenges.explanation: Izvini, gde je stanica? — Excuse me, where is the station?
challenges.translation: Excuse me, where is the station?

theory.title: A letter for each sound
theory.body: Serbian has 30 Cyrillic letters. A few familiar words show how the scripts line up: Здраво = Zdravo, Хвала = Hvala, Да = Da.

challenges.explanation: The two scripts spell the same Serbian word.

theory.title: A first conversation
theory.body: Kako si? asks “How are you?” informally. Dobro sam means “I am well.” For a polite or plural question use Kako ste?

challenges.explanation: Dobro sam is a common reply.
Use ste when addressing someone politely or more than one person.
You can answer Kako si? with Dobro sam.
You heard Kako si?, meaning How are you?.

theory.title: You can introduce yourself
theory.body: You can greet, say your name, ask how someone is, and read a few familiar Cyrillic words. Revisit any lesson you found tricky.

challenges.explanation: This is a friendly way to begin a conversation.
Добро сам means I am well.
Kako se zoveš? asks a name informally.
Molim is one of your most useful polite words.

theory.title: Show what you know
theory.body: This checkpoint reviews the unit. Answer at least 6 of 8 questions correctly to unlock the next unit. Listen again when you need to.

challenges.explanation: Zovem se Ana — My name is Ana
Kako si? asks how someone is.
Dobro sam means I am well.
Zovem se Ana — My name is Ana

units.title: Everyday essentials
units.subtitle: Numbers, time, cafés, family, and places
outcomes: Use basic time and number words

theory.title: First numbers
theory.body: Start with jedan (one), dva (two), and tri (three). Serbian number forms can change with noun gender; these forms are a first step.

challenges.explanation: Ovo je jedan pas. — This is one dog.
Ovo su dva psa. — These are two dogs.
Ovo su tri psa. — These are three dogs.

theory.title: Talk about when
theory.body: Danas means today, sutra means tomorrow, and sada means now. These words help you make simple plans.

challenges.explanation: Danas je ponedeljak. — Today is Monday.
Sutra je ponedeljak. — Tomorrow is Monday.
Sada sam kod kuće. — I am at home now.

theory.title: Order with a smile
theory.body: Kafa is coffee. When ordering one coffee, you can say Jednu kafu, molim. Voda means water; when ordering it, use vodu.

challenges.explanation: Kafu is used when coffee is the thing you order.
Jednu kafu molim — One coffee, please
Jednu kafu, molim is a polite order.

theory.title: People close to you
theory.body: Majka is mother, brat is brother, and sestra is sister. Moj is “my” with masculine nouns; moja goes with feminine nouns.

challenges.explanation: Sestra is feminine, so use moja.

theory.title: Find your way
theory.body: Gde? means “where?” Gde je stanica? asks “Where is the station?” Ovde means here, and tamo means there.

challenges.explanation: Gde je stanica — Where is the station?
Je means is in this question.
A simple question gets you a long way.
Gde je stanica — Where is the station?

theory.title: First present-tense phrases
theory.body: Radim means “I work.” Spavam means “I sleep.” Idem kući means “I am going home.” You can pair these with danas or sada.

challenges.explanation: Radim means I work; danas means today.
Idem kući means I am going home.
You heard radim, meaning I work.

theory.title: Show what you know
theory.body: This checkpoint reviews the unit. Answer at least 6 of 8 questions correctly to unlock the next unit. Listen again when you need to.

challenges.explanation: Jednu kafu, molim — One coffee, please
Jednu kafu, molim — One coffee, please
Kafu is the object form of kafa.
Gde je stanica? asks for the station.
Jednu kafu, molim — One coffee, please

units.title: My world
units.subtitle: Country, home, people and simple descriptions
outcomes: Understand basic vocabulary related to home and people
Describe your living situation and family
Use simple sentences to express personal details

theory.title: Where I live
theory.body: When describing where you live, use simple sentences. You can say 'Ja živim u...' followed by the name of the place.

challenges.explanation: Živim u gradu — I live in the city
Živim u gradu — I live in the city
Živim u gradu means I live in the city.

theory.title: My home
theory.body: To describe your home, use simple adjectives. You can say 'Moja kuća je...' followed by an adjective.

challenges.explanation: Moja kuća je velika — My house is big
Moja kuća je velika — My house is big
Moja kuća je velika means My house is big.

theory.title: People I know
theory.body: To talk about people you know, use phrases like 'On je moj prijatelj' or 'Ona je moja prijateljica'.

challenges.explanation: Ona je moja prijateljica — She is my friend
Ona je moja prijateljica — She is my friend
Ona je moja prijateljica means She is my friend.

theory.title: Describing things
theory.body: Use adjectives to describe nouns. For example, 'Ovo je lepa kuća'.

challenges.explanation: Ovo je lep park — This is a nice park
Ovo je lep park — This is a nice park
Ovo je lep park means This is a nice park.

theory.title: Family and pets
theory.body: To talk about family, use 'Moja porodica ima...' followed by family members or pets.

challenges.explanation: Imam psa — I have a dog
Imam psa — I have a dog
Imam psa means I have a dog.

theory.title: Personal details review
theory.body: This lesson reviews vocabulary and phrases from previous lessons. Practice using them in sentences.

challenges.explanation: Živim u Srbiji — I live in Serbia
Živim u Srbiji — I live in Serbia
Živim u Srbiji means I live in Serbia.

units.title: Food and shopping
units.subtitle: Ask for what you need at a café or shop.
outcomes: Use basic phrases for ordering food and drinks.
Ask for help in a shop or café.
Handle money and quantities in everyday situations.

theory.title: Food and Drink Vocabulary
theory.body: In this lesson, you will learn vocabulary related to food and drinks. Use these words to order at a café or shop.

challenges.explanation: Želim vodu means I want water.

theory.title: Meals Vocabulary
theory.body: In this lesson, you will learn vocabulary related to meals and breakfast. These words will help you talk about your daily meals.

challenges.explanation: Doručak je ukusan — Breakfast is tasty
Doručak je ukusan — Breakfast is tasty
Doručak je ukusan means Breakfast is tasty.

lessons.title: At a café
lessons.subtitle: Learn how to order at a café.

theory.title: Ordering at a Café
theory.body: In this lesson, you will learn how to order food and drinks at a café. Use polite phrases to ask for what you want.

challenges.explanation: Jednu kafu, molim — One coffee, please
Jednu kafu, molim means One coffee, please.

lessons.title: In a shop
lessons.subtitle: Learn how to shop for food.

theory.title: Shopping Vocabulary
theory.body: In this lesson, you will learn vocabulary related to shopping. Use these words to ask for items in a shop.

challenges.explanation: Koliko košta hleb? — How much does bread cost?
Koliko košta hleb? — How much does bread cost?
Koliko košta hleb? means How much does bread cost?.

theory.title: Money Vocabulary
theory.body: In this lesson, you will learn vocabulary related to money and quantities. This will help you in shopping situations.

challenges.explanation: Ovo je skupo — This is expensive
Ovo je skupo — This is expensive
Ovo je skupo means This is expensive.

theory.title: Review Vocabulary
theory.body: In this lesson, you will review vocabulary from previous lessons about food and shopping. This will help you remember the words.

challenges.explanation: Želim čaj means I want tea.

units.title: Around town
units.subtitle: Find places, travel and follow simple directions.

lessons.title: Places in town
lessons.subtitle: Learn about different places in your town.

theory.title: Places in town
theory.body: In this lesson, you will learn names of common places in a town. Use these words to ask for directions or to talk about where you want to go.

challenges.explanation: Gde je park? — Where is the park?
Gde je park? — Where is the park?
Gde je park? means Where is the park?.

theory.title: Left and right
theory.body: In this lesson, you will learn how to give directions using left and right. These words are essential for navigating in town.

challenges.explanation: Skrenite levo is a polite direction to turn left.

theory.title: Public transport
theory.body: In this lesson, you will learn about public transport vocabulary. This will help you when using buses or trams in the city.

challenges.explanation: Čekam autobus — I am waiting for the bus
challenges.translation: I am waiting for the bus

challenges.explanation: Čekam autobus — I am waiting for the bus
challenges.translation: I am waiting for the bus

challenges.prompt: I am waiting for the bus
challenges.explanation: Čekam autobus means I am waiting for the bus.

lessons.title: Tickets and journeys
lessons.subtitle: Learn how to talk about tickets and journeys.

theory.title: Tickets and journeys
theory.body: In this lesson, you will learn how to talk about tickets and journeys. This will help you when you need to buy a ticket or describe a journey.

challenges.explanation: Jednu kartu, molim — One ticket, please
Jednu kartu, molim — One ticket, please
Jednu kartu, molim means One ticket, please.

lessons.title: At the station
lessons.subtitle: Learn vocabulary for the train station.

theory.title: At the station
theory.body: In this lesson, you will learn vocabulary related to the train station. This will help you when you are at the station.

challenges.explanation: Voz polazi sada — The train leaves now
Voz polazi sada — The train leaves now
Voz polazi sada means The train leaves now.

theory.title: Review
theory.body: In this lesson, you will review all vocabulary learned in previous lessons. This will help you consolidate your knowledge.

challenges.explanation: Gde je stanica? — Where is the station?
Gde je stanica? — Where is the station?
Gde je stanica? means Where is the station?.

units.title: Everyday life
units.subtitle: Describe a simple day, work and study.
outcomes: Use basic phrases about daily activities.
Talk about time, days, and dates.

lessons.title: Morning and evening
lessons.subtitle: Daily routines in the morning and evening.

theory.title: Jutro i veče
theory.body: Ustajem means “I get up.” Use ujutru for “in the morning” and uveče for “in the evening.”

challenges.explanation: Ustajem rano — I get up early
Ustajem rano — I get up early
Ustajem rano means I get up early.

lessons.title: Days and dates
lessons.subtitle: Learn about days of the week and dates.

theory.title: Dani i datumi
theory.body: Serbian days of the week are written in lower case: ponedeljak, utorak, sreda, četvrtak, petak, subota, nedelja.

challenges.explanation: Danas je ponedeljak — Today is Monday
Danas je ponedeljak — Today is Monday
Danas je ponedeljak means Today is Monday.

theory.title: Na poslu
theory.body: Radim means “I work.” U školi means “at a school”; u introduces a location here.

challenges.explanation: Radim u školi — I work at a school
Radim u školi — I work at a school
Radim u školi means I work at a school.

theory.title: U školi
theory.body: Učim srpski means “I am learning Serbian.” Serbian often uses the present tense for actions happening now.

challenges.explanation: Učim srpski — I am learning Serbian
Učim srpski — I am learning Serbian
Učim srpski means I am learning Serbian.

theory.title: Hobiji i slobodno vreme
theory.body: Volim da čitam means “I like to read.” Use volim da before a present-tense verb for a common preference.

challenges.explanation: Volim da čitam — I like to read
Volim da čitam means I like to read.

theory.title: Ponavljanje svakodnevnog života
theory.body: Review simple present-tense statements, days, and familiar daily activities.

challenges.explanation: Sutra ne radim — I am not working tomorrow
Sutra ne radim — I am not working tomorrow
Sutra ne radim means I am not working tomorrow.

units.title: Health and weather
units.subtitle: Describe how you feel and talk about the weather.
outcomes: Talk about your body and health.

theory.title: Body Parts
theory.body: In Serbian, body parts are important vocabulary. Each part has a specific name. Knowing these helps in describing health.

challenges.explanation: Boli me glava — My head hurts
Boli me glava — My head hurts
Boli me glava means My head hurts.

theory.title: Expressing Feelings
theory.body: In Serbian, you can express how you feel using simple phrases. Use 'dobro' for good and 'loše' for bad.

challenges.explanation: Loše se osećam — I feel unwell
Loše se osećam — I feel unwell
Loše se osećam means I feel unwell.

theory.title: Pharmacy Vocabulary
theory.body: When visiting a pharmacy, knowing the right words is essential. You can ask for medicine or describe symptoms.

challenges.explanation: Treba mi lek — I need medicine
Treba mi lek — I need medicine
Treba mi lek means I need medicine.

theory.title: Weather Vocabulary
theory.body: Describing the weather is essential. Use simple adjectives to express conditions like sunny or rainy.

challenges.explanation: Danas je hladno — It is cold today
Danas je hladno — It is cold today
Danas je hladno means It is cold today.

lessons.title: Seasons and clothes
lessons.subtitle: Discuss seasons and what to wear.

theory.title: Seasons and Clothing
theory.body: Different seasons require different clothing. Knowing the words helps you dress appropriately.

challenges.explanation: Nosim jaknu — I am wearing a jacket
Nosim jaknu — I am wearing a jacket
Nosim jaknu means I am wearing a jacket.

theory.title: Review Vocabulary
theory.body: This lesson reviews vocabulary from previous topics. Practice using these words in sentences.

challenges.explanation: Dobro se osećam — I feel well
Dobro se osećam — I feel well
Dobro se osećam means I feel well.

units.title: Social life
units.subtitle: Make plans and exchange short messages.

lessons.title: Friends and neighbours
lessons.subtitle: Talk about your friends and neighbours.

theory.title: Talking about friends
theory.body: When talking about friends, use the names or pronouns. Use 'moj' for 'my' when talking about a male friend and 'moja' for a female friend.

challenges.explanation: Ovo je moj prijatelj — This is my friend
Ovo je moj prijatelj — This is my friend
Ovo je moj prijatelj means This is my friend.

theory.title: Making invitations
theory.body: Use phrases like 'Hoćeš li doći?' to invite someone. Respond with 'Da, dolazim' for acceptance or 'Ne, ne mogu' for refusal.

challenges.explanation: Hoćeš li doći? — Will you come?
Hoćeš li doći? — Will you come?
Hoćeš li doći? means Will you come?.

theory.title: Expressing likes and dislikes
theory.body: Use 'sviđa mi se' to express likes and 'ne sviđa mi se' for dislikes. You can also use nouns after these phrases.

challenges.explanation: Volim muziku means I like music.

theory.title: Talking on the phone
theory.body: Use phrases like 'Halo, kako si?' to greet someone on the phone. Ask questions to get information.

challenges.explanation: kako si means how are you.
čujem te means I hear you.
Čujemo se sutra means Talk to you tomorrow.

theory.title: Sending messages
theory.body: Use short phrases for messages. Keep it simple and clear. Use 'Hvala' for thank you and 'Vidimo se' for see you.

challenges.explanation: kako si means how are you.
Vidimo se uveče means See you this evening.

theory.title: Review of social life
theory.body: In this lesson, we will review phrases and vocabulary related to friends, invitations, likes, and short messages.

challenges.explanation: hoćeš li doći means will you come.
sviđa mi se means I like it.
Drago mi je means Nice to meet you.

units.title: Plans and memories
units.subtitle: Talk about simple plans and recent events.
outcomes: Understand and use simple future and past tenses.

lessons.title: Tomorrow and plans
lessons.subtitle: Learn to talk about your plans for tomorrow.

theory.title: Talking about tomorrow
theory.body: Sutra ću raditi means “I will work tomorrow.” Ću comes after sutra and before the infinitive raditi.

challenges.explanation: Sutra ću raditi — I will work tomorrow
Sutra ću raditi — I will work tomorrow
Sutra ću raditi means I will work tomorrow.

lessons.title: Future with ću
lessons.subtitle: Learn to use 'ću' for future actions.

theory.title: Using 'ću'
theory.body: For a simple future plan, say Ja ću kupiti kartu or Sutra ću kupiti kartu. The auxiliary changes with person.

challenges.explanation: Sutra ću kupiti kartu — I will buy a ticket tomorrow
challenges.translation: I will buy a ticket tomorrow

challenges.prompt: I will buy a ticket tomorrow
challenges.explanation: Sutra ću kupiti kartu means I will buy a ticket tomorrow.

lessons.title: Yesterday
lessons.subtitle: Learn to talk about what happened yesterday.

theory.title: Talking about yesterday
theory.body: Juče sam radio means “I worked yesterday” for a male speaker; a female speaker says radila.

challenges.explanation: Juče sam radio — I worked yesterday (male speaker)
Juče sam radio means I worked yesterday (male speaker).

lessons.title: Simple past
lessons.subtitle: Learn to use the simple past tense.

theory.title: Using the simple past
theory.body: In the past, sam combines with a past participle: kupio sam (male speaker), kupila sam (female speaker).

challenges.explanation: Juče sam kupio hleb — I bought bread yesterday (male speaker)
Juče sam kupio hleb — I bought bread yesterday (male speaker)
Juče sam kupio hleb means I bought bread yesterday (male speaker).

lessons.title: A weekend story
lessons.subtitle: Share a story about your weekend.

theory.title: Telling a weekend story
theory.body: Bili smo kod kuće means “We were at home.” This is a useful fixed phrase for a recent event.

challenges.explanation: Bili smo kod kuće — We were at home
Bili smo kod kuće — We were at home
Bili smo kod kuće means We were at home.

theory.title: Review of plans and memories
theory.body: Review simple future and past phrases. Use the gendered past form that fits the speaker.

challenges.explanation: Sutra ću učiti — I will study tomorrow
Sutra ću učiti — I will study tomorrow
Sutra ću učiti means I will study tomorrow.

units.title: Read and write
units.subtitle: Read both scripts and write short everyday texts.
outcomes: Understand and write basic Serbian in Cyrillic and Latin scripts.
Read and comprehend simple signs and notices.
Fill out basic forms in Serbian.

lessons.title: Cyrillic practice
lessons.subtitle: Learn to write and recognize Cyrillic letters.

theory.title: Cyrillic Alphabet
theory.body: Serbian uses both Latin and Cyrillic. The 30 printed Cyrillic letters correspond to Serbian sounds; practice reading them aloud.

challenges.explanation: б is b in Cyrillic and means b.

lessons.title: Reading signs
lessons.subtitle: Learn to read basic signs in Serbian.

theory.title: Understanding Signs
theory.body: You may see ИЗЛАЗ (izlaz, exit) and УЛАЗ (ulaz, entrance) on signs. Read the whole word.

challenges.explanation: Gde je izlaz? — Where is the exit?
Gde je izlaz? — Where is the exit?
Gde je izlaz? means Where is the exit?.

lessons.title: Filling a form
lessons.subtitle: Learn how to fill out a basic form in Serbian.

theory.title: Forms in Serbian
theory.body: Ime is first name, prezime is surname, and adresa is address. These labels may appear in either script.

challenges.explanation: Moje ime je Ana — My name is Ana
Moje ime je Ana — My name is Ana
Moje ime je Ana means My name is Ana.

lessons.title: A short notice
lessons.subtitle: Learn to write a short notice in Serbian.

theory.title: Writing Notices
theory.body: A notice may show datum (date), vreme (time), and mesto (place). Look for these key words first.

challenges.explanation: Sastanak je danas — The meeting is today
Sastanak je danas — The meeting is today
Sastanak je danas means The meeting is today.

lessons.title: A simple message
lessons.subtitle: Learn to write a simple message in Serbian.

theory.title: Writing Messages
theory.body: A short message can use Pozdrav, Hvala, or Vidimo se. Keep names and punctuation clear.

challenges.explanation: хвала is hvala in Cyrillic and means thank you.
Vidimo se sutra means See you tomorrow.

theory.title: Review
theory.body: Review reading and writing familiar words in both scripts.

units.title: A1 in real life
units.subtitle: Use your A1 skills in everyday situations.

theory.title: Introducing Yourself
theory.body: Use Zovem se... to give your name, then ask Kako se zoveš? when speaking informally.

challenges.explanation: Zovem se Ana — My name is Ana
Zovem se means My name is.

challenges.prompt: Write “Do you call yourself?” in Serbian
challenges.explanation: Se zoveš means Do you call yourself?.
Zovem se Ana means My name is Ana.

lessons.title: A café visit
lessons.subtitle: Learn to order food and drinks.

theory.title: Ordering in a Café
theory.body: At a café, request Jednu kafu, molim. Kafu is the object form of kafa.

challenges.explanation: Jednu kafu, molim — One coffee, please
Jednu kafu, molim means One coffee, please.

theory.title: Asking for Directions
theory.body: Ask Gde je stanica? for a station. Levo means left; desno means right.

challenges.explanation: Gde je stanica? — Where is the station?
Gde je stanica? — Where is the station?
Gde je stanica? means Where is the station?.

theory.title: Sending Messages
theory.body: Vidimo se sutra is a short, friendly message: “See you tomorrow.”

challenges.explanation: Kako si means How are you?.
Vidimo se sutra — See you tomorrow

challenges.prompt: Write “What are you doing?” in Serbian
challenges.explanation: Šta radiš means What are you doing?.
Vidimo se sutra means See you tomorrow.

theory.title: Reviewing A1 Skills
theory.body: Use familiar words from the course to describe the weather, your plans, and how you feel.

challenges.explanation: Danas je hladno — It is cold today
Danas je hladno — It is cold today
Danas je hladno means It is cold today.

theory.title: Your A1 knowledge check
theory.body: This assessment revisits introductions, everyday needs, directions, health, plans, listening and Cyrillic reading. Answer at least 10 of 12 questions correctly. It checks course knowledge, not spoken conversation.

challenges.explanation: Kako se zoveš? asks a name informally.
Где је станица? is Gde je stanica? in Cyrillic.
Jednu kafu, molim orders one coffee politely.
Živim u Srbiji means I live in Serbia.
Boli me glava means my head hurts.
Živim u Srbiji — I live in Serbia
Sutra ću raditi means I will work tomorrow.
Vidimo se sutra is a friendly goodbye.
Danas je hladno means it is cold today.
Gde je stanica? asks for the station.
